name: The Honey Drippers
hook: A funk band whose 1973 protest single against Nixon opened with a drum break that Marley Marl built 'The Bridge' on.
blurb: Roy C, a soul singer and producer whose full name is Roy Charles Hammond, wrote 'Impeach the President' in 1973, during the Watergate scandal that led to Richard Nixon resigning, and recorded it with a band called the Honey Drippers; when the band ended isn't sourced. The song starts with the drums on their own for a few bars. In 1986 Marley Marl took the kick and snare from those bars to build MC Shan's 'The Bridge', which accounts name among the first hip-hop records built on a sampled break rearranged into a new pattern. After that hundreds of other producers sampled them too: around 800 documented tracks. So a protest single about Nixon, stripped of its words, became one of the drum breaks hip-hop rests on.
